children: A routine four-hour journey between Riyadh and Kerala has turned into a travel ordeal lasting over 10 hours for some passengers, as they are forced to travel by road to Dammam or Bahrain to catch flights home.

Riyadh Airport has come under repeated attack from Houthi rebels, resulting in casualties and damage to airport facilities. As a precautionary measure, Indian carriers Air India, Air India Express, Akasa Air and IndiGo have suspended all flights to and from Riyadh until at least October 24. Saudi carriers, however, continue to operate services to India from Dammam, Jeddah and Medina.

The flight suspensions and resulting capacity cuts have significantly reduced seat availability, pushing up airfares. As a result, passengers needing to return to India urgently are travelling by bus or hiring cars to reach Buraydah, Dammam, or even Bahrain to board onward flights.
“Similarly, those who need to return to Riyadh before their visa entry deadlines expire are also travelling via Bahrain and the UAE,” a local resident said.

The road journey from Riyadh to Dammam or Bahrain takes between four and six hours, with both destinations located around 400-460 km  from the Saudi capital. However, travel to Jeddah is considerably longer, as the city is nearly 1,000 km  away.

The Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate General of India in Jeddah have activated 24x7 control rooms and are assisting Indian passengers seeking guidance. “The Consulate continues to engage with concerned local authorities, airlines, travel operators and Indian community volunteers to address difficulties faced by affected Indian nationals, including facilitating access to essential medicines, food and other necessary assistance,” it said in a post on X on Sunday evening.

Airlines are also attempting to ease the disruption for stranded passengers. While Saudia and flyadeal have re-routed some flights originally scheduled for Riyadh to Jeddah and Dammam, Air India Express is allowing passengers to rebook Saudi Arabia flight tickets free of charge to any other Gulf destination.
Charter flights are also being arranged to help affected travellers.

“We are organising charter flights from Jeddah to Kochi. Bus services between Riyadh and Jeddah are operating normally. The charter flights will also support passengers stranded in Riyadh,” said Biju Varughese, Director (Holidays) at Alhind Tours and Travels.

title: From runway to highway: Stranded Riyadh passengers take the long road home
